goal:
`kvconf get` fails on a value that has a `#` inside double quotes. With this file:

```
[app]
title = "Issue #42: retry"
```

`go run ./cmd/kvconf get app.conf app.title` prints `kvconf: line 2: unterminated quoted value` instead of `Issue #42: retry`.

A `#` inside a double-quoted value is part of the value. The other quoting rules in the README must keep working:

- an unquoted value still ends at the first `#`: `port = 8080 # http` gives `8080`;
- after the closing quote, `# ...` is a comment: `title = "x" # note` gives `x`;
- inside quotes, `\"` is a double quote and `\\` is a single backslash: `path = "C:\\temp"` gives `C:\temp`.

`checks/quoted-hash.sh` reproduces the problem. The tests run with `go test ./...`.

criteria.statement: `kvconf get` prints `Issue #42: retry` for the reported file
criteria.baseline: it must fail on the input snapshot, reproducing the problem; interlock saw it fail there (run run-20c9c30cdbb14b39)

criteria.statement: Every quoting rule in the task holds: a # inside quotes is kept, an unquoted value ends at #, a comment may follow the closing quote, and \" and \\ are escapes inside quotes

criteria.baseline: it must pass on the input snapshot, as a regression guard; interlock saw it pass there (run run-619680918fa342c3)

previous_result.summary:
I changed `parseValue` in `parser.go` so a `#` inside double quotes stays part of the value. Quoted values are now scanned character by character. `\"` and `\\` are unescaped, and the closing quote may be followed only by whitespace or a `# ...` comment. Unquoted values still end at the first `#`.

One behaviour change you didn't ask for: text after a closing quote that isn't a comment, such as `"x" y`, now gives an "unexpected text after quoted value" error. Before, that input gave "unterminated quoted value".

I added `TestQuotedValues` to `parser_test.go`, covering all four rules from the brief plus a mixed case. `sh checks/quoted-hash.sh` now prints `Issue #42: retry`, and `go test ./...` passes. I recorded claims for repro (observed), regression (tested) and spec (tested). The spec criterion still needs an independent verifier.
